findings.evidence:
app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml line 6 declares <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.USE_EXACT_ALARM" /> alongside SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM. The app is a task/routine planner (com.dalgeer.lifeplanner) using exact alarms for task and routine reminders in AlarmScheduler.kt.

**Critic Verification**: AndroidManifest.xml line 6 declares android.permission.USE_EXACT_ALARM. Under Google Play Policy, USE_EXACT_ALARM is restricted to apps whose primary core function is an alarm clock, timer, or calendar app with event reminders. As a task and routine planner, LifePlanner does not qualify for USE_EXACT_ALARM and must rely exclusively on SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM. (Confidence: High)
findings.issue_summary: The app requests the restricted 'android.permission.USE_EXACT_ALARM' permission in AndroidManifest.xml, but as a productivity task and routine planner, it does not qualify for this permission under Google Play policy.
findings.recommendation: Remove <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.USE_EXACT_ALARM" /> from app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml. Rely instead on android.permission.SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM with runtime checks using PermissionUtils.canScheduleExactAlarms().
